title: Eisenhower's 1961 farewell names a military-industrial complex
summary: Eisenhower's 1961 farewell, as Avalon prints it, uses the phrase military-industrial complex.
body: Avalon prints Eisenhower's 1961 farewell under the title of the military-industrial complex speech. The phrase is in the address as published on that page. The speech is a warning from a departing president, not a statute creating or abolishing any industry. The wording on the page includes: "1700 - 1799 19th Century 1800 - 1899 20th Century 1900 - 1999 21st Century 2000 - Military-Industrial Complex Speech, Dwight D. Eisenhower, 1961 My fellow Americans: Three days from now, after half a century in the service of our country, I shall lay down the responsibilities of office as, in traditional and solemn ceremony, the authority of the Presidency is".
